identity_evidence.captured_title: You are the Deep Research source-base reviewer for NebulaMind's galaxy-evolution wiki rebuild. Queue item 05 of 20 Core review: Maiolino, Roberto & Mannucci, Filippo (2019), The Astronomy and Astrophysics Review, volume 27, article 3, "De re metallica: the cosmic chemical evolution of galaxies." Verified review identity to confirm: DOI 10.1007/s00159-018-0112-2; arXiv 1811.09642; ADS bibcode 2019A&ARv..27....3M. Mission purpose Build a large, authoritative, advisory source base from this review so three independent methods can later build galaxy-evolution wiki pages from zero. Extract the review's bounded synthesis and harvest important primary papers it actually cites. This is not live-wiki prose and authorizes no database, trust, claim, evidence, deployment, publication, or account mutation beyond this one Deep Research run. Temporal and topical boundary - Use the 2019 review and primary literature it actually cites. - Do not promote post-2019 papers as if the review cited them. - Maintain the queue's non-AGN focus. AGN contamination or ionization may be mentioned only where needed to bound galaxy metallicity diagnostics. Quarantine AGN demographics, accretion physics, and AGN-only papers from the core harvest. - Later sources and AGN-centered sources may appear only in DO_NOT_USE_UNVERIFIED. Scientific scope 1. Metal production, stellar yields, nucleosynthetic channels, time delays, IMF dependence, recycling, and chemical-evolution bookkeeping. 2. Gas-phase, stellar, neutral-gas, CGM, and intracluster metallicity tracers and how these phases differ. 3. Direct electron-temperature methods, recombination lines, strong-line methods, photoionization models, calibration offsets, dust depletion, ionization parameter, and abundance-scale systematics. 4. Galaxy mass-metallicity relations, luminosity-metallicity relations, stellar-metallicity relations, secondary SFR dependence/FMR, gas fractions, and redshift evolution. 5. Spatially resolved metallicity gradients, central dilution, bars, mergers, inflows, outflows, mixing, and environmental effects. 6. Relative abundance ratios such as alpha/Fe, N/O, C/O, and their clocks, yields, and diagnostic ambiguities. 7. Metal budgets, effective yields, enriched outflows, metal retention, CGM reservoirs, and missing metals. 8. Chemical-evolution models and cosmological simulations: assumptions, calibrated inputs, predictions, and unresolved degeneracies. 9. High-redshift limitations, selection effects, line accessibility, stacking, spatial resolution, and local-analog assumptions. Required output 1. Review identity and scope map - Confirm exact title, authors, year, journal, DOI, arXiv, and ADS bibcode. - Map authorized scientific territory and explicit exclusions. - Preserve phase, tracer, calibration, sample, redshift, IMF, and abundance-scale boundaries. 2. Established findings - At least 12 atomic entries with IDs [REV05-E01], ... - For every entry include role, epistemic_type, one bounded finding, physical/sample/calibration boundary, review section/topic basis, confidence note, and source keys. - Allowed epistemic types: observation | analytic_theory | hydrodynamic_simulation | semi_analytic_model | calibration | review_synthesis. - Never collapse gas-phase, stellar, CGM, and neutral-gas metallicities into one interchangeable quantity. 3. Open debates and tensions - At least 8 entries with IDs [REV05-D01], ... - Include competing positions, why unresolved in 2019, boundaries, and source keys. - Include: direct-method versus strong-line abundance scale; empirical versus theoretical calibrations; primary/secondary N production and N/O; reality/form of the FMR; inflow versus outflow control of MZR; gradient flattening/inversion; yield/IMF/time-delay degeneracies; and high-redshift diagnostic evolution. 4. Key measurements, model benchmarks, and calibrations - At least 8 entries with IDs [REV05-N01], ... - Include exact value/equation when the review supplies it; units; phase/tracer/calibration/sample/redshift/IMF; whether observed, assumed, calibrated, or predicted; caveat; and source keys. - Useful targets: solar oxygen reference, calibration discrepancies, MZR slopes/turnovers/scatter, FMR parameterizations, metallicity evolution, gradient units, alpha/Fe timescales, effective-yield relations, and metal-budget fractions. Include only values bound to cited sources and review context. 5. What remained unknown in 2019 - At least 6 entries [REV05-U01], ... with the gap, why it matters, needed observation/model test, and source keys. 6. Primary-citation harvest - Harvest 40-80 important PRIMARY papers actually cited by Maiolino & Mannucci 2019. - Balance across diagnostic methods/calibrations, local and high-z scaling relations, FMR and counter-results, gradients/mixing, abundance ratios, yields/chemical theory, simulations, neutral/CGM metals, and metal budgets. - Supporting reviews/books may be listed separately but must not count toward the primary total. - Exclude post-2019 papers, uncited search results, aggregators, and AGN-only papers. - One physical paper per source key; no duplicates. - IDs [REV05-P001], [REV05-P002], ... - Each row: [REV05-PNNN] Authors (year, journal) | title=exact title | DOI:value-or-none; arXiv:value-or-none; ADS:value | role=measurement|analytic_theory|hydrodynamic_simulation|semi_analytic_model|calibration | review_locator=section/topic | one-line boundary - If an identifier or review membership is uncertain, quarantine the row rather than making it usable. Composite identifier discipline - First author/year/title/DOI/arXiv/ADS must name the same physical paper. - The paper must actually appear in the review bibliography. - Never splice neighboring reference identifiers. - Use none when an identifier genuinely does not exist. - Calibration papers must identify the exact abundance scale they establish or compare. 7. DO_NOT_USE_UNVERIFIED - Quarantine uncertain, cross-wired, uncited, post-2019, AGN-centered, phase-collapsing, or overbroad items. - Format: UNCITED_NOT_USABLE | candidate or claim | supplied identifier/context | exclusion reason - Explicitly quarantine claims that all metallicity calibrations share one absolute scale, gas and stellar metallicity are directly interchangeable, the FMR is universal and redshift-invariant, one gradient measures all phases, or matching the MZR validates one feedback model. - Quarantine post-2019/JWST/ML browsing results. 8. Review and source identity ledger - Repeat review as [REV05-R00] with DOI/arXiv/ADS. - Repeat every usable primary and supporting row with author/year/journal, DOI, arXiv, ADS, role, and boundary. - No load-bearing source may be absent from this ledger. Quality bar - Advisory source base, not polished wiki prose. - Prefer explicit phase/tracer/calibration boundaries over broad claims. - Preserve observed versus modeled, calibrated versus predicted, and total versus gas-phase versus stellar abundances. - Every source key in findings/debates/measurements/unknowns must resolve in the usable ledger. - End exactly: REVIEW_BASE_05_DR_COMPLETE_REFERENCE_ONLY
